title: Sliding-window KV tiling memory profiles for Llama/Mistral/Qwen long-context variants
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce per-model, sliding-window ‘tiling’ memory profiles that reduce peak GPU working set for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants while preserving continuous-batching throughput and KV cache hit-rate. This ticket explores a tiling strategy where KV residency is managed as overlapping tiles aligned to typical sequence windows (e.g., 2k/4k/16k), with soft eviction boundaries to minimize re-population cost under interleaved batching.
background: We observe that for long-context variants, static per-layer residency allocations lead to high fragmentation and worst-case peaks when many long sequences align across requests. Existing per-variant slices reduce mean footprint but suffer when request alignments change or batch mixing occurs. Continuous batching introduces temporal locality: tokens appended to active conversations tend to cluster in time. We aim to exploit that locality with sliding tiles that maintain high locality for active conversations and shrink non-active tiles proactively.
acceptance_criteria: Memory peak reduction >= 18% on 8k/16k synthetic workload compared to baseline per-variant profile
End-to-end P99 token latency increase <= 6% under steady-state continuous batching
KV cache hit-rate drop <= 2 percentage points versus baseline for mixed-length production traces
Automated profiler + heatmap added to Console per-model dashboard (tile residency view)
PR with runtime changes, unit tests, and integration benchmark added to CI with perf regression checks
implementation_notes: Introduce concept of KV tiles: contiguous KV address ranges with metadata: residency_score, last_access_ts, overlap_ratio
Eviction policy: soft-trim with overlap preservation (retain N overlapping tokens across tile boundary) to avoid frequent re-population on shifts
Admission policy: cheap heuristic to promote tiles when sequence tail activity exceeds threshold across recent batching window
Per-model tuning knobs: tile_size_candidates (e.g., 512, 1024, 2048), overlap_fraction (e.g., 10-25%), shrink_factor for idle tiles
Integration with batching: when batching merges requests with tails that map into adjacent tiles, prefer to keep tiles resident to avoid tail thrash
Fallback: if memory pressure is severe, fall back to current slab allocator behavior; ensure safety checks prevent OOM
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed comparing static slices vs sliding tiles on Llama-8k; sliding tiles show 14% peak reduction in microbenchmarks (local test rig, 40% batch mix).
2026-03-04: Prototype tile metadata added to runtime; implemented last_access_ts and simple LRU across tiles. Observed unexpected thrash at high concurrency due to eviction timing misalignment.
2026-03-07: Introduced overlap_fraction and soft-trim (keep 256 tokens across boundaries). Thrash reduced; KV hit-rate improved by ~3% on synthetic interleaved trace.
2026-03-10: Benchmarked on Mistral-16k variant using continuous batching harness. Peak memory down 19% but end-to-end P99 increased 9% — identified extra mutex contention in tile admission path.
2026-03-12: Reworked admission hot path to use per-stream preallocated token ranges (lock-free read-mostly); P99 regression reduced to 4%. Preparing PR for internal review.
design_decisions: Prefer overlapping tiles over strict fixed slices to preserve locality when sequences shift by a few hundred tokens.
Use soft eviction (trim but keep overlap) rather than hard eviction to reduce re-warm cost for continuous batching workloads.
Expose tile_size_candidates per-model, but provide sane defaults discovered from profiler heatmaps; do not make tile sizes fully dynamic in this iteration to limit complexity.
Admission heuristics should be batching-aware: count active tails per recent time window rather than absolute token counts to avoid promoting tiles from bursty noise.
open_questions: What are sensible defaults for overlap_fraction across model families? (A/B: 10% vs 20%)
Should we allow tiles to be migrated between GPUs in Dedicated clusters when hot-spots move, or is that premature complexity?
How to present tile residency and overlap to Console UX for troubleshooting without overwhelming users?
Impact on quantized kernels: do some tiling layouts interact poorly with 4-bit kernel alignments? Need microbench.
test_plan: Unit tests for tile metadata correctness and eviction invariants; integration at CI: run continuous batching harness with production traces (1h), verify acceptance criteria metrics; add perf guard to CI that blocks regressions > 5% on P99 or > 10% on peak memory.
rollout_plan: Gate behind runtime-1.20 feature flag. Canary rollout to 5% of traffic on hosted tier with detailed tracing enabled (tile residency logs). If metrics stable after 24h, ramp to 25% then 100% over a week. For Dedicated, provide optional opt-in config and run with customer test dataset prior to enabling.
notes: This ticket focuses on the first pass: single-host tile residency management and batching-aware heuristics. Follow-up tickets will explore cross-GPU migration, per-layer adaptive tile sizes, and Console UX for tile visualization.
